newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH BARBARIANS REPEAT WIN OVER SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH BARBARIANS REPEAT WIN OVER SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Fine place kicking by full-back Sebastien Viars made the difference as the French Barbarians beat South Africa for the second time in succession with a 30-22 win in the Springboks' opening French tour match on Saturday.
Viars missed just one kick as he landed three conversions and three penalties for a personal tally of 15 points.
The Springboks, fielding their second string side, suffered their first defeat of a three-country tour that began in Argentina earlier this month.
South Africa scored four tries but fly-half Franco Smith's kicking was poor, landing only one conversion, that of Theo Oosthuizen's first try.
Springbok coach Andre Markgraaff, whose side meet France in the first test in Bordeaux next Saturday, said on Friday that South Africa hoped to win all five matches on French soil.
Instead the Barbarians were again a thorn in Springbok flesh after winning the last match of South Africa's previous tour of France in 1992 which marked the farewell of French great Serge Blanco.

The Barbarians, with the world's most-capped test player Philippe Sella in the backs, ran in three tries in some fine sweeping movements in stark contrast to the Springboks' tries, all but one worked by the forwards.
The home side never looked back after hooker Marc Dal Maso put them in front with a try in the first minute. The closest South Africa came to the Barbarians was 10-7 down after Oosthuizen scored.

Oosthuizen scored a second and number eight Johan Erasmus added another but full-back Russell Bennett's was the sweetest after a sweeping counter-attack that began in the forwards and switched to the backs where he took a pass from Smith.
For the Barbarians, winger David Venditti touched down after a astute kick ahead by centre Guillaume Bouic.
Fly-half Laurent Mazas, a late replacement for Toulouse's Christophe Deylaud, scored in the corner to cap a well-worked backline movement.
New Zealand flanker Josh Kronfeld, who played for the French side, said: "There's nothing quite like beating the Boks."

French Barbarians - 15-Sebastien Viars; 14-Franck Corrihons (17-Michel Marfaing 30), 13-Philippe Sella, 12-Guillaume Bouic, 11-David Venditti (16-David Arrieta); 10-Laurent Mazas, 9-Fabien Galthie; 8-Thierry Labrousse, 7-Marc Lievremont (captain), 6-Josh Kronfeld, 5-Marc Cecillon (18-Gregory Kacala 72), 4-Ross Grant (19-Mike James 68), 3-Mauricio Reggiardo (20-Richard Crespy 72), 2-Marc Dal Maso (21-Jean-Michel Gonzalez 60), 1-Pierre Triep-Capdeville.

Springboks - 15-Russell Bennett; 14-Andries Snyman, 13-Jeremy Thomson, 12-Dick Muir, 11-Joe Gillingham; 10-Franco Smith, 9-Kevin Putt; 8-Johan Erasmus, 7-Theo Oosthuizen (19-Krynauw Otto 62), 6-Wayne Fyvie (captain), 5-Frederick van Heerden, 4-Hannes Strydom (20-James Dalton 60), 3-Marius Hurter, 2-Henry Tromp, 1-Garry Pagel (21-Toks van der Linde 61).
